patient_information: A 55-year-old female pig farmer from rural Vietnam with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, on treatment for 4 years.
history_of_present_illness: A 55-year-old woman presented with a 1-day history of fever, headache and vomiting; her blood film was negative for malaria and she was treated with fluids and paracetamol; on the second day of illness, she developed confusion and was referred for further investigation.
exposure_and_epidemiology: She raises pigs on her smallholding and works as a butcher in a local market selling pork and chicken in rural Vietnam, a malaria-endemic area.
vitals: Glasgow Coma Score of 12/15 (E3 M5 V4), fever (38.5°C or 101.3°F), tachycardia (124 bpm), hypotension (85/60 mmHg), tachypnoea (32 breaths per minute), and hypoxia (O2 saturation 86% on ambient air).
physical_exam: She is confused, has neck stiffness and photophobia, no focal neurological signs, a diffuse petechial rash over her trunk, and marked purpuric non-blanching lesions on her left leg; the rest of her examination is unremarkable.
labs_and_diagnostics: Non-contrast-enhanced CT scan of the brain is unremarkable; electrocardiogram shows sinus tachycardia and is otherwise normal; chest x-ray is unremarkable; admission laboratory results are detailed in Table 85.1; CSF analysis revealed turbid fluid with 2870 cells/µL, 92% neutrophils, protein 541.16 mg/dL, glucose 2.44 mmol/l, and a CSF/serum glucose ratio of 0.12; Gram stain showed a Gram-positive coccus in short chains; negative India ink, mycobacterial GeneXpert, Herpes simplex virus PCR, repeat malaria film, and malaria rapid diagnostic tests.
differential_diagnosis: Severe malaria, enteric fever, dengue fever, melioidosis, acute bacterial meningitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae), Streptococcus suis infection, tuberculous meningitis, and cryptococcal meningitis.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient received empirical treatment with intravenous ceftriaxone and vancomycin, and supportive treatment including intravenous fluids; dexamethasone was administered for the first 4 days of treatment; she responded to treatment but had residual bilateral hearing impairment after 12 days of antibiotic therapy.
